title: De Soto's expedition through the southeastern United States
summary: Hernando de Soto landed near Tampa Bay in 1539 with a Spanish force and marched north and west through the southeast. The expedition wintered at Anhaica, passed through Georgia and South Carolina in 1540, fought at Mobila, and crossed the Mississippi River in May 1541; de Soto died of fever on 21 May 1542.

uncertainty.note: The Mariners' Museum dates the landing to May 25, 1539 and the Mississippi crossing to May 1541; the National Park Service gives May 1539 and dates the Congaree-area stop (Hymahi) to April 26, 1540. The USF map page titles the route 1539-1542. The Mississippi crossing and the later Arkansas winter are not plotted because no opened page gives a locatable point.

importance.justification: The first large Spanish expedition into the interior of the southeastern United States, with lasting effects on the Native peoples met.

audience_note: Describes violence against Native peoples, including the burning of an inhabitant during questioning, fighting at Mobila, and enslavement and killing in earlier raids in Central America.

beats.caption: De Soto lands near Tampa Bay in May 1539, winters at the Apalachee town of Anhaica, and marches northeast into Georgia and the Carolinas.
In 1540 the expedition reaches the Congaree area, then Mobila near Mobile, where it fights the local people.
After crossing the Mississippi River in May 1541, de Soto dies of fever on 21 May 1542, leaving the expedition without its leader.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the Mobile point is only 'near present-day Mobile' on the opened page, so the 100 km uncertainty is a floor and the real site is debated; Anhaica is plotted at Tallahassee. The western leg to the Mississippi is left unplotted for lack of a locatable stop. The consequence caption follows the page's death date and does not claim what happened next. The record id carries 1541 for the Mississippi crossing.
